_note: Chrome for design/marketing/Search.dc.html at /search. The search page already had search_placeholder, idle_summary, popular_heading and empty_sub; the design's three remaining literals had no CMS home. These rows add the results-summary line the design composes in JS (`${total} result${s} for "${q}"` — seeded as a plural and a singular row with {n}/{q} tokens the page substitutes at render time, the same way the project-type detail chrome substitutes {name}/{short}), the empty-state heading `No results for "{q}"` (same {q} token), and the three empty-state browse chips (All services / Project types / By city), which the design points at Services.dc.html, Projects.dc.html and Cities.dc.html and which map to the real /services, /projects and /cities routes in the Next app. Popular search terms and the result groups themselves come from the search endpoint, not from copy.
